flagged.title: How Minerals Form
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly presents the metamorphic index mineral sequence as mica transforming into chlorite with increasing heat/pressure, reversing the Barrovian sequence.

mark_affecting.quote: those clay minerals transform into mica. At even more heat and pressure, and the mica transforms into chlorite.

flagged.title: Igneous Rocks: Texture, Mineralogy and Classification
flagged.reason: The video teaches incorrect GCSE specification grain-size boundaries (>1 mm instead of >3 mm for coarse) and teaches a fundamentally wrong geological rule that euhedral crystals indicate slow cooling rather than order of crystallisation.

mark_affecting.quote: Because they have time, the crystals grow large, greater than 1 millimeter across. That gives us a coarse-grained texture

If the crystals look angular, jagged and messy, that firmly points to fast cooling. But if you see beautifully geometric, smooth, well-formed crystals, that indicates slow cooling. The proper scientific term for a well-formed crystal is euhedral... euhedral crystals in a photomicrograph are a massive clue that the magma cooled slowly deep underground.

flagged.title: Sedimentary Rocks and Environments of Deposition
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly describes the Carboniferous cyclothem sequence as running upwards from coal to shale to limestone, completely inverting the standard shallowing-upward sequence and omitting sandstone, which would cause students to lose marks on cyclothem questions.

mark_affecting.quote: It starts at the bottom with coal... Right beneath that coal is the seat earth... But then sea levels rise, the swamp gets flooded, bringing in low-energy marine conditions that deposit shale. As the water gets even deeper and clearer, limestone is deposited on top.
